Saint Pulcheria

Pulcheria · St. Aelia Pulcheria · St. Pulcheria the Empress · St. Empress Pulcheria

Period
Fourth–fifth centuries; died 453
Region
Constantinople; Byzantine Empire
Titles / vocation
Righteous · Ruler
Commemoration
September 10

Introduction

Saint Pulcheria was a Byzantine empress who supported Orthodox teaching, church building, and the councils of Ephesus and Chalcedon.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Peaceful repose in 453

Read circumstances and sources

Background

She was a daughter of Emperor Arcadius and sister of Theodosius II. The OCA describes her as her brother’s coregent and adviser, with a broad education and an active commitment to Orthodox teaching.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Opening paragraph on Arcadius, TheodosiusIIand education

Life and notable events

Court conflict temporarily removed her from power. After returning, and after her brother’s death, she married the new emperor Marcian. The received life says that the marriage preserved her chosen virginity. She also supported churches and monasteries.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Paragraphs on withdrawal, return and marriage to Marcian

Death and martyrdom

The life records her giving wealth to the poor and the Church. She died peacefully in 453 at the age of 54. It does not describe martyrdom.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Final paragraph on almsgiving and repose

Writings and legacy

Her legacy in the cited source concerns patronage and defense of Orthodox doctrine, particularly around Ephesus in 431 and Chalcedon in 451. These were episcopal councils; her support did not turn the empress herself into a bishop or the author of their definitions.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Paragraphs on Ephesus431,Chalcedon451andchurchpatronage
